newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures spent a lacklustre session stuck in a similar range to last Friday while long-dated cash bonds suffered from some non-resident sales helping the five-year zone of the curve outperform slightly.

The September bond future started the day in a positive mood but came under consistent pressure from traders pushing it lower through a series of technical levels in what was the quietest session for more than a month.
Traders said Tuesday's session looked destined to be another range-bound, technically driven day, with movements in the German and U.S. bond markets likely to provide the direction.

Talk of a strong June inflation figure from the German state of Bavaria added to the bearish tone in the afternoon but the fears were eventually proved unfounded when the released showed a 0.2 percent rise, sparking short covering late in the day.
The contract settled up 0.04 at 128.66 but the 10-year benchmark bond yield rose two basis points to 5.65, lagging its German counterpart slightly.

An analyst at a French brokerage said remarks from French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn that the new government would avoid a sharp rise in the 1997 deficit were not enough to remove investors' concerns about French public finances.

An analyst at a London brokerage said some non-resident investors had been lightening their long-term holdings of French bonds, mainly on concerns about a large deficit in 1997, and moving into dollar-denominated bonds. "We've seen movements out of francs into dollars and that play is being put on by long-term holders of French bonds," he said.
A trader at a large French bank said there had been some non-resident selling of bonds with maturities of 10-years and longer on Monday.
September PIBOR also remained in a fairly narrow range with support at 96.52 continuing to hold. It settled up one basis point at 96.54.
The French franc was little changed at 3.3734 at 1537 GMT compared with 3.3727 late on Friday.
The Treasury announced it would be issuing a new 10-year OAT, a 5.5 percent October 25, 2007 bond, at its next monthly auction on July 3.
